title: Linear-time computation implies polynomial time
statement: Let $f$ be a function on bit strings. If there exist a finite binary Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $a$ such that, on every input of length $n$, $M$ computes $f$ in time $a(n+1)$, then $f$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps bit strings to bit strings.
There exist a finite binary Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $a$.
$M$ computes $f$ on every input within $a(n+1)$ steps, where $n$ is the input length.
replaced: Let $f$ be a function from bit strings to bit strings. If there are a finite binary Turing machine $M$ and a constant $a \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $M$ computes $f$ within $a(n+1)$ steps on every input of length $n$, then $f$ is polynomial-time computable, i.e.\ some finite binary Turing machine computes $f$ within $C(n+1)^c$ steps on every input of length $n$, for some constants $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$.
